user.title: Set up KDE for Home Assistant
user.description: Home Assistant found the files of the older KDE Connect integration. You can take over its pairings, so your devices stay paired.

import_legacy.title: Take over existing pairings
import_legacy.description:
These devices stay paired: {devices}.

Remove the older KDE Connect integration before you continue. Both use the same network ports, so only one of them can run.

data_description.name: The name your devices show for Home Assistant.

abort.single_instance_allowed: KDE for Home Assistant is already set up. Open **KDE for Home Assistant** in the sidebar to add a device.
abort.import_failed: The files of the older integration could not be read. Choose **Start fresh** instead.
abort.legacy_running: The older KDE Connect integration is still running. Both use the same network ports, so remove it first, restart Home Assistant and try again.

error.legacy_running: Remove the older KDE Connect integration first, then try again.

create_entry.default: Home Assistant now shows up as a KDE Connect device on your network. [Open KDE for Home Assistant in the sidebar](/{path}) to add your computers and phones step by step.

pick.title: Choose a device
pick.description: Found {count} unpaired devices. Make sure KDE Connect is running on the device and that it is on the same network as Home Assistant.

manual.title: Enter the address
manual.description: Use this when the device is not found automatically, for example when it is on another network.

data_description.host: The IP address or hostname of the device.

data_description.mac: Needed to turn the device on with Wake-on-LAN. Leave empty to hide the wake up button.
data_description.scripts: These scripts show up under Run command in KDE Connect on the device.

progress.discover: Looking for KDE Connect devices on your network.
progress.connect: Waiting for the device to connect to Home Assistant.
progress.pair:
Accept the pairing request on **{name}** within 30 seconds. If no notification appears, open KDE Connect on the device and select **Accept**.

Verification key: **{key}**

abort.not_loaded: KDE for Home Assistant is not running. Check the integration page for errors and try again.
abort.cannot_connect: The device did not connect to Home Assistant. Check that KDE Connect is running on the device and that the device can reach Home Assistant on TCP ports 1716 to 1764.
abort.pair_timeout: The pairing request was not accepted in time. Try again and accept it on the device.
abort.pair_rejected: The device declined the pairing request.

data_description.name: The name your devices show for Home Assistant.

not_connected.message: {name} is not connected to Home Assistant.

port_in_use.message: Could not open the KDE Connect network ports ({error}). If the older KDE Connect integration is still installed, remove it and restart Home Assistant.

device_unpaired.title: {name} is no longer paired
device_unpaired.description:
{name} removed its pairing with Home Assistant, so Home Assistant can no longer control it.

To fix this, delete the device from the KDE for Home Assistant integration and pair it again.
